title: How the Panama Canal Lifts Ships Using Gravity
voice: Grady voice not generated; paid credits require authorization
footage_license: Candidate federal-public-domain material; no grant until actual clip verified
narration: How can ships climb 26 meters without a crane? At the Panama Canal's original locks, giant gates close behind each vessel. Water flows through tunnels inside the lock walls and floor. Gravity carries water from a higher level into the chamber. As the water rises, the ship floats up with it. When the levels match, the next gate opens. This is a massive water elevator powered by gravity.
